newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian railway workers stage 10-day strike.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian railway workers stage 10-day strike.

text.p: Slovenian railway workers started a 10-day strike on Tuesday to press for higher salaries and holiday pay, leaving cargo transport crippled in the west of the country but passenger transport unaffected.

"Passengers on Slovenian trains have not suffered any damage so far as only cargo trains are stopped just in Slovenia's western stations," Olga Zvanut, spokeswoman for Slovenian Railways, told Reuters.
The rail strike is the fifth to hit the tiny Alpine nation this year after two one-hour and two four-hour warning strikes by railway workers earlier.
Some 2,810 employees out of a total 9,655 employed on the railroads will participate in the strike to demand a 14 percent increase in wages and 70 percent more holiday pay.
Franc Pavlic, a spokesman for the strikers, said the strike will spread if demands are not met.
"If our demands are not met by May 24, complete railway traffic in Slovenia will be blocked," Pavlic said.
Currently the average gross monthly wage of a railway worker is about 128,000 tolars ($826), below the average of 138,593 tolars.
The government and the company's management had offered to increase holiday pay to 80,000 tolars from 74,000 tolars last year.
The government said it could not agree to wage increases as the state-owned railway posted a 3.6 billion tolars loss in 1996, down from a profit of 68 million in the previous year.
The railway strike follows a series of strikes last year, which eventually pushed the government into concessions before the general election in November.
